## TRA Timeline

#### IPO origination

- 2005-02-14: Form of Tax Receivable Agreement filed as Exhibit 10.4 to S-1/A (unexecuted draft, 85% pay-over of excess Hypothetical over Actual Tax Liability).
- 2005-02-22: Executed TRA dated February 22, 2005, between Cendant Corporation, Cendant Mobility Services Corporation, and Wright Express Corporation, filed on 8-K (2005-02-16).

#### Cendant separation and Realogy prepayment

- 2006: Cendant separation reallocates the TRA payment stream as a Cendant Contingent Asset (Realogy 62.5%, Wyndham 37.5%); WEX's obligation unchanged.
- 2009-06-26: Tax Receivable Prepayment Agreement: WEX pays Realogy $51M lump sum against $187M carrying value to extinguish Realogy's allocated share. Ratification Agreement same date confirms residual pay-over to Wyndham at 31.875% (= 37.5% of 85%).

#### Economic decay

- 2017-12-31: TCJA-driven $15.3M non-cash reduction; federal rate cut from 35% to 21% reduces the Hypothetical Tax Liability and thus future pay-overs.
- 2020-12-31: Last disclosed balance of $2.0M; 2021 10-K onward shows only the exhibit listing, no footnote balance.

## Explanation

The WEX TRA originated at the February 2005 IPO, when Wright Express LLC was converted into Wright Express Corporation immediately before the offering and the resulting basis step-up generated future tax savings owed to Cendant Corporation. WEX agreed to pay 85% of the excess of its Hypothetical Tax Liability (computed without the step-up) over its Actual Tax Liability. The 2006 Cendant separation reassigned the payment stream to Realogy and Wyndham as successor beneficiaries; in June 2009 WEX prepaid Realogy's 62.5% share for $51M, leaving Wyndham as the sole remaining counterparty at an effective 31.875% pay-over. The carrying value then decayed steadily, with the 2017 TCJA driving a $15.3M one-time step-down as the lower 21% corporate rate reduced future Hypothetical Tax Liabilities. The last reported balance is $2.0M at year-end 2020; the TRA remains an exhibit in the 2025 10-K by incorporation, but the economic obligation has effectively run off without a formal termination instrument. See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record.
